title: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Model (LLM) (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5 (GPT-5)) for Meniscal Tear Detection on Knee Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): A Pilot Study

model.params_source: assumed (paper states only the model id and the default service tier; reasoning effort and verbosity not stated; temperature not settable)

task.subset_rule: seeded random 100 cases (seed 20260907) from the MRNet validation set (120 exams): 50 meniscal-tear positive, 50 negative, requiring complete sagittal and coronal series (resolution plan)
task.approximation: the paper's 100 cases and its quality exclusions are not listed; slices are min-max normalized to PNG as described; image detail parameter not stated; the comparison is set-level and should fall inside the reported CI

items.source: MRNet (Stanford AIMI), https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ (registration and data-use agreement required): valid/sagittal/*.npy, valid/coronal/*.npy, valid-meniscus.csv
items.filter: complete sagittal and coronal series; adequate image quality (manual check in the paper)

fields.input: sagittal series (20-44 slices) and coronal series as 256x256 PNGs
fields.label: valid-meniscus.csv label (1 = tear)

items.license: MRNet Dataset Research Use Agreement (registration required)

prompt.user_template: Analyze these knee MRI images (coronal and sagittal views) and determine whether meniscal tear presents. Respond only with 'yes' or 'no'.

placeholders.<images>: all slices of the sagittal series followed by all slices of the coronal series, attached as image parts of the same user message (one request per case)

output.parse: label from set [yes, no]: first occurrence (case-insensitive)
output.postprocess: strip, lowercase; neither word -> counted as incorrect and reported

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: fraction of the 100 cases whose yes/no equals the meniscal-tear label
metric.original_location: Results / Table 1: accuracy 0.76 (95% CI 0.668-0.833), sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.68

open_points: no hook: MRNet is gated (Stanford AIMI research-use agreement, ~5.8 GB) and every request carries 40-88 image parts; the runner builds text-only messages.
image detail level (low/high) is not stated; confirm that all slices fit one gpt-5 request.
if the validation set has fewer than 50 positive meniscal-tear cases, decide the class balance.
notes: Each request carries two series (40-88 images); at low detail ~85 tokens per image, ~$0.02-0.07 per call. The paper's precision 0.72 / recall 0.84 / F1 0.78 follow from the same predictions.
